notes: T547 (concurrent workers share one git index) — pass-with-findings. The one-writer invariant protects FILE CONTENTS, not the git index: two rows can legally hold disjoint files and still collide at commit time, because `git add <path>` stages that path's ENTIRE current working-tree content (which may be another row's in-flight edit) and .git/index is one shared mutable file with no lock held across a worker's stage→commit sequence. T521's 784235a (self-reported) absorbed T531/T545's build.zig hunks + T512's regression-dispatch.sh arms under the T521 message; d7e4bdb is the same class from the Orchestrator seat. TWO MECHANISMS BUILT, both in tools/git-commit-mine. (1) COMMIT MUTEX: an exclusive flock(2) via fd 9 (python3 fcntl — bash 3.2 on this host has no flock(1), and the fd-9-via-python pattern was proven to hold the lock after the child exits because the bash fd keeps the open file description alive) is taken around the whole stage→verify→commit span and released on every exit path — the EXIT trap closes fd 9, and flock is kernel-released on ANY process death (crash/SIGKILL/exit 1), so there is no stale-lock wedge. Lock file is $REPO/docs/infra/managent/git-commit-mine.lock, ALONGSIDE the store's own tasks.json.lockfile and NOT inside .git/ (the bundle's instruction); it is gitignored (added docs/infra/managent/git-commit-mine.lock to .gitignore) so the runtime-created file never pollutes git status. Default acquisition BLOCKS until the holder finishes (the holder WILL finish — flock cannot go stale); GCM_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECS bounds the wait for tests/diagnostics and turns a timeout into a loud refusal. Released explicitly right after `git commit` lands (before the read-only post-commit verification) to keep the held window minimal. (2) HOLDS CHECK: before staging, every named path is compared against the live holders map (gcm_active_holders: holds ∪ bundle-deliverables of in_progress rows, T539-populated). A path held by a DIFFERENT in_progress row (or, when the commit is unlabelled, by any in_progress row) is REFUSED with the holder's id + agent named, BEFORE any staging, so the index stays byte-for-byte untouched; --explicit bypasses the refusal but prints a loud WARNING naming the holder (the escape is recorded, not silent). An unreadable store degrades to warn-and-allow (T540 item 3), consistent with the pre-commit backstop, so a momentarily-unreadable kanban never wedges a worker. WORKTREE-PER-WORKER JUDGEMENT (the bundle required a decision, recorded either way): CHOSE THE MUTEX, not per-worker worktrees. Reasons: (a) a mutex is ~1 flock syscall + one lock file vs a worktree's ~200–500 ms clone + disk per worker + a mandatory merge step on every row close; (b) worktrees would make the two fleet-coordination surfaces (docs/status/CURRENT.md, HANDOVER.md) and the two absorption surfaces (CLAIMS.md, rejections.json) that every worker legitimately touches become cross-worktree merge conflicts by design — the mutex keeps one tree and lets those shared surfaces stay shared; (c) the merge step reintroduces attribution ambiguity at the boundary, the exact disease this task exists to cure; (d) the fleet already operates with one checkout and the wrapper is the single commit choke-point, so one lock there closes the index race for the whole fleet without touching any worker's workflow. A worktree-per-worker design remains the right STRUCTURAL fix if the fleet ever moves to heavier parallelism or a worker needs long-lived isolation, and should be an ADR if pursued; it is not needed for the current concurrency. SHARED-STATE HAZARD REPORT (bundle item 4 — checked, changed only where needed): .git/index.lock — CONFIRMED HAZARD, FIXED AS A SIDE EFFECT: the pre-mutex null arm (two concurrent disjoint commits, no injected delay) failed deterministically enough to observe with `git add` dying on the other process's index.lock; the mutex serializes stage→commit, so no two wrapper processes run `git add`/`git commit` concurrently and the contention is gone (arm 5 now green). .git/HEAD — read-mostly during a commit (git updates it under .git/HEAD.lock inside the commit, which the mutex already serializes); no wrapper path mutates HEAD outside `git commit`, so no separate action. The stash — NOT touched by the wrapper; it remains a shared ref and manual `git stash` from two consoles can still interleave, but nothing in the commit path uses it, so it is out of scope for this mechanism and reported rather than changed. The store lockfile (tasks.json.lockfile) — managent's flock is independent of the commit mutex; a commit mutating the index and a managent write mutating tasks.json do not contend, which is correct (different files, different serialization domains).
